intended_object: The category of finite locally free O_X-modules (vector bundles) of constant rank r on a scheme X, as a full subcategory of the finite locally free sheaves. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
`FixedRank X r` is the full subcategory of `FiniteLocallyFreeSheaf X` (itself the full subcategory of `X.Modules` cut out by `isFiniteLocallyFree`) on the objects E with `E.rank x = r` for every point x. `rank` is the locally constant function sending x to the cardinality of a finite basis of E on an open neighbourhood of x, and Rank.lean proves it does not depend on the choice of basis. This is the standard notion of a locally free sheaf of rank r, i.e. a rank-r vector bundle, and taking the full subcategory with all O_X-linear maps as morphisms is standard. On the empty scheme the condition holds vacuously, which is also correct. The library proves that the property is closed under isomorphism and under pullback, and that rank one gives exactly the invertible sheaves, which is consistent with the intended meaning.

The definition is stated for schemes. Locally free sheaves of rank r also make sense on ringed spaces, but the whole library works with `Scheme.Modules`, and for schemes this is a standard setting. Mathlib (at this commit) has no notion of locally free sheaves of a given rank to compare against: a grep for `IsLocallyFreeOfRank`, `LocallyFreeOfRank` and `isFiniteLocallyFree` found nothing. So the definition is not too narrow.
